## Step 7: Nested-model checks and model validation

This step assesses whether all components of the two-factor Schwartz–Smith (2000) model are empirically required by estimating and comparing restricted versions of the model to the unrestricted benchmark. Rather than assuming that every parameter is necessary, the paper emphasizes testing whether specific structural features materially improve model fit.

Three restricted models are considered. First, the correlation between shocks to the short-term and long-term factors is removed. Second, the market price of risk associated with the short-term factor is set to zero. Third, both restrictions are imposed simultaneously. Each restricted model is re-estimated using maximum likelihood and evaluated using likelihood-ratio tests and the Akaike Information Criterion.

The results indicate that allowing for correlation between the two latent factors is important. Removing this correlation leads to a statistically significant loss in fit and a higher information criterion, confirming that short-term deviations and long-run movements in prices are linked. In contrast, setting the short-term risk premium to zero does not significantly worsen model performance, suggesting that this component plays a limited role.

Overall, these findings closely match the conclusions of Schwartz and Smith (2000). The interaction between the short-term and long-term factors is a core feature of the model, while the short-term risk premium can be omitted without materially reducing explanatory power.

```{r step7, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#############################################################################
# STEP 7 — Nested-model checks (LR tests & AIC)
#############################################################################

# Required objects (created by S&S 2000 Full Timeline and loaded above) ---
stopifnot(
  exists("theta_hat_SS_FullTimeline_V2.0"),
  exists("Y"), exists("Tau"), exists("Delta_t"),
  exists("best"), is.list(best), !is.null(best$par),
  exists("loglik"), exists("pack"), exists("unpack")
)


# Full-model packed parameter vector at the optimum (S&S 2000 Full Timeline)
# best$par is the vector that was actually optimized (so it matches loglik() exactly)
p_full_hat <- best$par

# Helper: compute POSITIVE log-likelihood from a packed vector p
# In the S&S 2000 Full Timeline convention, loglik(...) returns the NEGATIVE log-likelihood
LL_from_p <- function(p) {
  -as.numeric(loglik(p, Y = Y, Tau = Tau, Delta_t = Delta_t))
}

LL_full  <- LL_from_p(p_full_hat)
k_full   <- length(p_full_hat)                # total number of estimated packed params
AIC_full <- -2 * LL_full + 2 * k_full         # standard AIC

# --- 1) Identify packed indices robustly (NO hard-coded packing order) -------
# We locate "which element of p moves rho / lambda_chi" by small perturbations.
# This avoids assuming any specific pack() ordering or transformation details.
infer_p_index_for <- function(target_name, p0, eps = 1e-6) {
  th0 <- unpack(p0)
  stopifnot(target_name %in% names(th0))  # must be a natural parameter returned by unpack()

  base_val <- th0[[target_name]]
  deltas   <- numeric(length(p0))

  for (i in seq_along(p0)) {
    p1 <- p0
    p1[i] <- p1[i] + eps                     # tiny bump in ONE packed coordinate
    th1 <- unpack(p1)
    deltas[i] <- abs(th1[[target_name]] - base_val)  # how much did the natural value move?
  }

  # If everything is ~0, something is wrong (e.g., target_name not actually linked to p)
  if (max(deltas, na.rm = TRUE) <= 0) {
    stop("Could not infer packed index for: ", target_name,
         " (no sensitivity detected).")
  }

  which.max(deltas)
}

# For our Step-7 tests we need indices for rho and lambda_chi
idx_rho        <- infer_p_index_for("rho",        p_full_hat)
idx_lambda_chi <- infer_p_index_for("lambda_chi", p_full_hat)

# --- 2) Map natural-scale "fixes" -> packed fixed values --------------------
# Key trick:
#   - Start from unpack(p_full_hat) (natural θ)
#   - Overwrite θ[[name]] = target
#   - pack(θ) gives a packed vector consistent with the parameter constraints/transforms
#   - fixed packed value is just p_fixed[idx_*]
packed_value_for_fix <- function(name, value, p0) {
  th <- unpack(p0)
  stopifnot(name %in% names(th))

  # Overwrite the NATURAL parameter (e.g., rho = 0)
  th[[name]] <- value

  # Re-pack using the S&S 2000 Full Timeline pack() (so transforms are handled correctly)
  p_new <- pack(th)

  # Return both the full vector and the specific packed coordinate value
  list(p_new = p_new, val_at = NA_real_)
}

# Convenience wrapper: return ONLY the fixed packed value at a given index
fixed_val_at_index <- function(name, value, p0, idx) {
  th <- unpack(p0)
  th[[name]] <- value
  p_new <- pack(th)
  as.numeric(p_new[idx])
}

# --- 3) Generic restricted fit: hold selected packed indices fixed ----------
# We keep a "template" full vector, then optimize only the FREE coordinates.
fit_restricted <- function(fix_natural, p_start = p_full_hat) {
  # fix_natural: named list like list(rho = 0) or list(rho = 0, lambda_chi = 0)
  stopifnot(is.list(fix_natural), length(fix_natural) >= 1)

  # Template is the full vector we will overwrite each evaluation
  p_template <- p_start

  # Build fixed-index and fixed-value vectors (packed space)
  fixed_idx <- integer(0)
  fixed_val <- numeric(0)

  for (nm in names(fix_natural)) {
    # Decide which packed index corresponds to this natural parameter
    idx <- switch(
      nm,
      "rho"        = idx_rho,
      "lambda_chi" = idx_lambda_chi,
      stop("This Step 7 currently supports only fixes for: rho, lambda_chi. Got: ", nm)
    )

    # Compute the packed value consistent with setting nm to the target natural value
    val <- fixed_val_at_index(nm, fix_natural[[nm]], p0 = p_start, idx = idx)

    fixed_idx <- c(fixed_idx, idx)
    fixed_val <- c(fixed_val, val)
  }

  fixed_idx <- as.integer(fixed_idx)
  fixed_val <- as.numeric(fixed_val)

  # FREE coordinates are everything except the fixed ones
  free_idx <- setdiff(seq_along(p_template), fixed_idx)

  # Starting point for the free vector = the full optimum restricted to free coordinates
  p_free0 <- p_template[free_idx]

  # Objective in free coordinates:
  #   - assemble full p
  #   - insert free values
  #   - overwrite fixed coordinates
  #   - return NEGATIVE logLik (because loglik() already returns neg logLik)
  obj_free <- function(p_free) {
    p_full <- p_template
    p_full[free_idx]  <- p_free
    p_full[fixed_idx] <- fixed_val
    loglik(p_full, Y = Y, Tau = Tau, Delta_t = Delta_t)
  }

  opt <- optim(
    par     = p_free0,
    fn      = obj_free,
    method  = "BFGS",
    control = list(maxit = 4000, reltol = 1e-10)
  )

  # Reconstruct final full packed vector at restricted optimum
  p_hat <- p_template
  p_hat[free_idx]  <- opt$par
  p_hat[fixed_idx] <- fixed_val

  list(
    opt       = opt,
    p_full    = p_hat,
    theta     = unpack(p_hat),              # natural-scale restricted estimate
    logLik    = LL_from_p(p_hat),           # positive LL
    k_free    = length(free_idx),           # number of FREE parameters
    fixed     = fix_natural
  )
}

# --- 4) Run the standard nested-model checks --------------------------------
# R1: rho = 0            (no correlation between chi/xi innovations)
fit_r1 <- fit_restricted(list(rho = 0))

# R2: lambda_chi = 0     (no market price of risk for chi)
fit_r2 <- fit_restricted(list(lambda_chi = 0))

# R3: rho = 0 & lambda_chi = 0 (both restrictions at once)
fit_r3 <- fit_restricted(list(rho = 0, lambda_chi = 0))

# --- 5) Likelihood-ratio tests + AIC table ---------------------------------
# LR statistic: 2*(LL_full - LL_restricted)
# df: number of restrictions = (k_full - k_free_restricted)
lr_row <- function(name, fit_res) {
  LR  <- 2 * (LL_full - fit_res$logLik)

  # df = (#params in full) - (#free params in restricted)
  # because restricted model estimates only k_free parameters (the rest are fixed)
  df  <- k_full - fit_res$k_free

  p   <- pchisq(LR, df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)

  tibble(
    model   = name,
    logLik  = fit_res$logLik,
    k_free  = fit_res$k_free,
    AIC     = -2 * fit_res$logLik + 2 * fit_res$k_free,
    LR_stat = LR,
    df      = df,
    p_value = p
  )
}

tab_lr <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble(
    model   = "Full",
    logLik  = LL_full,
    k_free  = k_full,
    AIC     = AIC_full,
    LR_stat = NA_real_,
    df      = NA_integer_,
    p_value = NA_real_
  ),
  lr_row("R1: rho = 0",                    fit_r1),
  lr_row("R2: lambda_chi = 0",             fit_r2),
  lr_row("R3: rho = 0 & lambda_chi = 0",   fit_r3)
)

print(tab_lr)

# Optional: quick view of what the restricted estimates look like (natural scale)
print(fit_r1$theta)
print(fit_r2$theta)
print(fit_r3$theta)

```

## Step 8: Out-of-Sample One-Step-Ahead Forecast Evaluation

Step 8 evaluates the out-of-sample forecasting performance of the Schwartz–Smith (2000) two-factor model in a realistic, real-time setting. The sample is split into training and test periods, where model parameters are estimated using only historical data available in the training window. The estimated parameters are then held fixed during the test window, and the Kalman filter is used to generate one-step-ahead forecasts. Forecast errors are measured by the Kalman innovations, allowing the computation of standard accuracy metrics such as RMSE and MAE across maturities. This procedure ensures that forecasting performance reflects genuine predictive power rather than in-sample fit.

Methodologically, this approach closely follows the state-space framework proposed by Schwartz and Smith (2000). After estimating the model parameters via maximum likelihood on the training data, the Kalman filter is applied to infer the latent short-term and long-term factors. The filtered state at the end of the training window serves as the initial condition for forecasting in the test period. During the test window, the model updates only the latent state in response to new observations, while the structural parameters remain unchanged. This design mimics how the model would be used by a practitioner who must forecast future prices based solely on information available at the time.

The results for normal market periods indicate strong out-of-sample performance and limited overfitting. In the earlier normal window, one-month contracts exhibit an out-of-sample RMSE of approximately 0.11 compared to an in-sample RMSE of about 0.07, while longer maturities show smaller errors and narrower gaps between in-sample and out-of-sample performance. In the later normal period, the difference between in-sample and out-of-sample RMSE becomes even smaller, particularly for medium and long maturities. These findings suggest that the model captures the persistent component of the futures curve effectively and that parameter estimates remain stable over time in tranquil market conditions.

In contrast, the crisis-period results reveal a sharp deterioration in forecasting accuracy, especially at short maturities. For example, during the stress window, the one-month contract shows a large increase in out-of-sample RMSE relative to its in-sample counterpart, while longer maturities are less affected. This pattern is consistent with the economic structure of the Schwartz–Smith model, in which short-dated prices are dominated by transitory shocks that become highly volatile during periods of market stress. The pronounced out-of-sample errors at the front end therefore reflect genuine unpredictability rather than model misspecification.

Overall, Step 8 demonstrates that the Schwartz–Smith model performs well in stable environments while transparently revealing its limitations during extreme market conditions. The out-of-sample framework confirms that the model generalizes well in normal times and that forecast errors increase in a systematic and economically interpretable way during crises. By explicitly comparing in-sample and out-of-sample performance across maturities and regimes, Step 8 provides a rigorous validation of the model’s empirical relevance and clarifies where its forecasting strengths and weaknesses lie.

```{r step8, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
###############################################################################
# STEP 8 — OOS evaluation (FINAL, robust, S&S 2000 Full Timeline compatible)
###############################################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tibble)
  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(FKF)
})


# ============================= Preconditions ================================

stopifnot(
  exists("Y"), is.matrix(Y),
  exists("Tau"),
  exists("obs_dates"), length(obs_dates) == ncol(Y),
  exists("Delta_t"), is.finite(Delta_t), Delta_t > 0
)

dates_all <- as.Date(obs_dates)
data_lo   <- min(dates_all)
data_hi   <- max(dates_all)

mats_lab <- if (exists("ranks") && length(ranks) == nrow(Y)) {
  paste0(ranks, "m")
} else {
  paste0(seq_len(nrow(Y)), "m")
}

# Ensure `contracts` exists for sample_start()
if (!exists("contracts")) {
  # Option A: use the canonical 5 SS(2000) contracts
  contracts <- c("CL1 Comdty", "CL5 Comdty", "CL9 Comdty", "CL13 Comdty", "CL17 Comdty")
}

# Safety check: must match the data dimension used in training
stopifnot(length(contracts) == nrow(Y))

# ============================= Utilities ====================================

clamp_window <- function(s, e) {
  s <- max(as.Date(s), data_lo)
  e <- min(as.Date(e), data_hi)
  if (s > e) return(NULL)
  c(s, e)
}

# -------- robust theta estimation: choose best numerically stable fit --------
fit_theta_train <- function(Y_train, Tau_train,
                            n_starts = 10, seed = 42, maxit = 400,
                            rho_max = 0.995) {

  set.seed(seed)
  p0s <- replicate(n_starts, pack(sample_start()), simplify = FALSE)

  fits <- purrr::map(p0s, function(p0) {
    tryCatch(
      optim(p0, fn = loglik,
            Y = Y_train, Tau = Tau_train, Delta_t = Delta_t,
            method = "BFGS",
            control = list(maxit = maxit, reltol = 1e-10)),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
  })

  fits <- purrr::keep(fits, ~ !is.null(.x) &&
                        is.finite(.x$value) &&
                        all(is.finite(.x$par)))

  if (length(fits) == 0) {
    stop("STEP 8: all optimizer starts failed (non-finite likelihood/params).",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  ord <- order(purrr::map_dbl(fits, "value"))
  fits <- fits[ord]

  best_abs_rho <- Inf

  for (k in seq_along(fits)) {
    theta <- tryCatch(unpack(fits[[k]]$par), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(theta)) next

    must <- c(theta$kappa, theta$sigma_chi, theta$sigma_xi, theta$rho,
              theta$lambda_chi, theta$mu, theta$mu_star, theta$sigma_obs_vec)
    if (!all(is.finite(as.numeric(must)))) next
    if (theta$kappa <= 0 || theta$sigma_chi <= 0 || theta$sigma_xi <= 0) next
    if (any(theta$sigma_obs_vec <= 0)) next

    best_abs_rho <- min(best_abs_rho, abs(theta$rho))

    if (abs(theta$rho) > rho_max) next

    return(theta)
  }

  stop(sprintf(
    "STEP 8: all candidate fits had |rho| > %.3f (closest |rho| = %.6f).",
    rho_max, best_abs_rho
  ), call. = FALSE)
}

# -------- safe prior (regression prior or diffuse fallback) ------------------
get_prior_safe <- function(masked_train, L_use = 6) {
  L_use <- min(L_use, ncol(masked_train$yt))

  pr <- tryCatch(
    compute_prior_from_first_L(masked_train$Zt,
                               masked_train$ct,
                               masked_train$yt,
                               L = L_use, inflate = 2.0),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(pr) ||
      any(!is.finite(pr$m0)) ||
      any(!is.finite(pr$P0))) {
    return(list(m0 = c(0,0), P0 = diag(1e6, 2)))
  }
  pr
}

# ============================= Core runner ==================================

run_oos_section <- function(section_name,
                            train_start, train_end,
                            test_start,  test_end,
                            n_starts = 10, seed = 42) {

  tr <- clamp_window(train_start, train_end)
  te <- clamp_window(test_start,  test_end)

  if (is.null(tr) || is.null(te)) {
    message(sprintf("[%s] Skipped (window outside data).", section_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  is_train <- dates_all >= tr[1] & dates_all <= tr[2]
  is_test  <- dates_all >= te[1] & dates_all <= te[2]

  if (!any(is_train) || !any(is_test)) {
    message(sprintf("[%s] Skipped (empty slice).", section_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  Y_train   <- Y[,  is_train, drop = FALSE]
  Tau_train <- Tau[, is_train, drop = FALSE]
  Y_test    <- Y[,  is_test,  drop = FALSE]
  Tau_test  <- Tau[, is_test,  drop = FALSE]

  if (ncol(Y_train) < 20) {
    message(sprintf("[%s] Skipped (training window too short).", section_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # (1) Estimate theta on TRAIN (robust selection)
  theta_train <- fit_theta_train(
    Y_train, Tau_train,
    n_starts = n_starts, seed = seed
  )

  # (2) TRAIN filter
  ss_tr <- make_ss_arrays(theta_train, Tau_train, Delta_t)
  masked_tr <- apply_missing_mask_fkf(Y_train, ss_tr)
  pr <- get_prior_safe(masked_tr, L_use = 6)

  kf_tr <- fkf(
    a0  = pr$m0, P0 = pr$P0,
    dt  = masked_tr$dt, ct = masked_tr$ct,
    Tt  = masked_tr$Tt, Zt = masked_tr$Zt,
    HHt = masked_tr$HHt, GGt = masked_tr$GGt,
    yt  = masked_tr$yt
  )

  if (mean(is.finite(kf_tr$vt)) < 0.7) {
    stop(sprintf("[%s] TRAIN innovations mostly non-finite.", section_name),
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  # (3) TEST filter (1-step-ahead forecasts)
  # FKF updates the first supplied observation before applying a transition, so
  # a0/P0 must be the predicted a_{T+1|T}, P_{T+1|T} (as in the strategy code),
  # not the filtered a_{T|T}, P_{T|T}.
  aT <- kf_tr$at[, ncol(Y_train) + 1L]
  PT <- kf_tr$Pt[,, ncol(Y_train) + 1L]

  if (any(!is.finite(aT)) || any(!is.finite(PT))) {
    stop(sprintf("[%s] Non-finite end-of-train state.", section_name),
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  ss_te <- make_ss_arrays(theta_train, Tau_test, Delta_t)
  masked_te <- apply_missing_mask_fkf(Y_test, ss_te)

  kf_te <- fkf(
    a0  = as.numeric(aT), P0 = PT,
    dt  = masked_te$dt, ct = masked_te$ct,
    Tt  = masked_te$Tt, Zt = masked_te$Zt,
    HHt = masked_te$HHt, GGt = masked_te$GGt,
    yt  = masked_te$yt
  )

  if (mean(is.finite(kf_te$vt)) < 0.7) {
    stop(sprintf("[%s] TEST innovations mostly non-finite.", section_name),
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  # (4) Metrics
  rmse_oos <- sqrt(rowMeans(kf_te$vt^2, na.rm = TRUE))
  mae_oos  <- rowMeans(abs(kf_te$vt), na.rm = TRUE)
  rmse_in  <- sqrt(rowMeans(kf_tr$vt^2, na.rm = TRUE))

  oos_tbl <- tibble(
    maturity = mats_lab,
    RMSE_OOS = rmse_oos,
    MAE_OOS  = mae_oos
  )

  compare_tbl <- oos_tbl %>%
    mutate(RMSE_in_sample_train = rmse_in,
           OOS_minus_in_sample  = RMSE_OOS - RMSE_in_sample_train)

  cat(sprintf("\n===== %s =====\n", section_name))
  print(oos_tbl)
  print(compare_tbl)

    invisible(list(
    # summary tables
    oos_tbl     = oos_tbl,
    compare_tbl = compare_tbl,

    # --- ADD: everything needed for Step-6-style OOS visuals (no recompute) ---
    meta = list(
      section_name = section_name,
      train_window = tr,
      test_window  = te
    ),
    theta_train = theta_train,

    # data slices
    dates_test  = dates_all[is_test],
    Y_test      = Y_test,
    Tau_test    = Tau_test,

    # state-space arrays for TEST (needed for Z_t, c_t in measurement equation)
    ss_te       = ss_te,

    # Kalman filter outputs
    kf_tr       = kf_tr,
    kf_te       = kf_te
  ))

}

# ============================= Four sections ================================

res_norm1 <- run_oos_section(
  "Section 1 — Normal A (Train 1990–2004, Test 2005–2014)",
  "1990-01-01","2004-12-31",
  "2005-01-01","2014-12-31"
)

res_norm2 <- run_oos_section(
  "Section 2 — Normal B (Train 2005–2014, Test 2015–2024)",
  "2005-01-01","2014-12-31",
  "2015-01-01","2024-12-31"
)

res_cris1 <- run_oos_section(
  "Section 3 — Crisis 1 (Train 2003–2007, Test 2008)",
  "2003-01-01","2007-12-31",
  "2008-01-01","2008-12-31"
)

res_cris2 <- run_oos_section(
  "Section 4 — Crisis 2 (Train 2017–2019, Test 2020)",
  "2017-01-01","2019-12-31",
  "2020-01-01","2020-12-31"
)

step8_multi_outputs <- list(
  normal_1 = res_norm1,
  normal_2 = res_norm2,
  crisis_1 = res_cris1,
  crisis_2 = res_cris2
)


###############################################################################
# STEP 8 ADD-ON — OOS 1-step-ahead forecasts with 2/3 TRAIN – 1/3 TEST split
###############################################################################

# --- A) Define split (time-ordered) -----------------------------------------
T_all   <- ncol(Y)
T_train <- floor((2/3) * T_all)
T_test  <- T_all - T_train
stopifnot(T_train >= 20, T_test >= 10)

idx_train <- 1:T_train
idx_test  <- (T_train + 1):T_all

cat(sprintf("Total T=%d | Train=%d | Test=%d\n", T_all, T_train, T_test))
cat(sprintf("Train range: %s to %s\n", dates_all[1], dates_all[T_train]))
cat(sprintf("Test  range: %s to %s\n", dates_all[T_train + 1], dates_all[T_all]))

Y_train_23   <- Y[, idx_train, drop = FALSE]
Tau_train_23 <- Tau[, idx_train, drop = FALSE]
Y_test_13    <- Y[, idx_test,  drop = FALSE]
Tau_test_13  <- Tau[, idx_test, drop = FALSE]

# --- B) Estimate theta on 2/3 TRAIN (same robust estimation as Step 8) -------
theta_23 <- fit_theta_train(
  Y_train_23, Tau_train_23,
  n_starts = 10, seed = 42
)

# --- C) Filter TRAIN to get end-of-train state ------------------------------
ss_tr_23    <- make_ss_arrays(theta_23, Tau_train_23, Delta_t)
masked_tr_23 <- apply_missing_mask_fkf(Y_train_23, ss_tr_23)
pr_23       <- get_prior_safe(masked_tr_23, L_use = 6)

kf_tr_23 <- FKF::fkf(
  a0  = pr_23$m0, P0 = pr_23$P0,
  dt  = masked_tr_23$dt, ct = masked_tr_23$ct,
  Tt  = masked_tr_23$Tt, Zt = masked_tr_23$Zt,
  HHt = masked_tr_23$HHt, GGt = masked_tr_23$GGt,
  yt  = masked_tr_23$yt
)

if (mean(is.finite(kf_tr_23$vt)) < 0.7) {
  stop("[2/3–1/3] TRAIN innovations mostly non-finite.", call. = FALSE)
}

T_train_eff <- ncol(masked_tr_23$yt)
# Predicted a_{T+1|T}, P_{T+1|T} for the first test week (see Step 8 runner).
aT1_T_23 <- kf_tr_23$at[,  T_train_eff + 1L]
PT1_T_23 <- kf_tr_23$Pt[,, T_train_eff + 1L]

if (any(!is.finite(aT1_T_23)) || any(!is.finite(PT1_T_23))) {
  stop("[2/3–1/3] Non-finite end-of-train state.", call. = FALSE)
}

# --- D) Run TEST (1/3) recursion --------------------------------------------
ss_te_13     <- make_ss_arrays(theta_23, Tau_test_13, Delta_t)
masked_te_13 <- apply_missing_mask_fkf(Y_test_13, ss_te_13)

kf_te_13 <- FKF::fkf(
  a0  = as.numeric(aT1_T_23),
  P0  = PT1_T_23,
  dt  = masked_te_13$dt, ct = masked_te_13$ct,
  Tt  = masked_te_13$Tt, Zt = masked_te_13$Zt,
  HHt = masked_te_13$HHt, GGt = masked_te_13$GGt,
  yt  = masked_te_13$yt
)

if (mean(is.finite(kf_te_13$vt)) < 0.7) {
  stop("[2/3–1/3] TEST innovations mostly non-finite.", call. = FALSE)
}

# --- E) Forecast accuracy summary (same style as Step 8) ---------------------
rmse_oos_13 <- sqrt(rowMeans(kf_te_13$vt^2, na.rm = TRUE))
mae_oos_13  <- rowMeans(abs(kf_te_13$vt), na.rm = TRUE)
rmse_in_23  <- sqrt(rowMeans(kf_tr_23$vt^2, na.rm = TRUE))

oos_tbl_23_13 <- tibble(
  maturity = mats_lab,
  RMSE_OOS = rmse_oos_13,
  MAE_OOS  = mae_oos_13
)

compare_tbl_23_13 <- oos_tbl_23_13 %>%
  mutate(RMSE_in_sample_train = rmse_in_23,
         OOS_minus_in_sample  = RMSE_OOS - RMSE_in_sample_train)

cat("\n===== ADD-ON — 2/3 TRAIN → 1/3 TEST =====\n")
print(oos_tbl_23_13)
print(compare_tbl_23_13)

# (Optional) store in the same list
step8_multi_outputs$split_2over3_1over3 <- list(
  oos_tbl = oos_tbl_23_13,
  compare_tbl = compare_tbl_23_13
)



```

### Visual Representation

**Out-of-sample visual evaluation of the term structure.**\
This extension to Step 8 provides a visual out-of-sample assessment of the Schwartz–Smith (2000) model by examining how well the estimated model predicts the cross-sectional shape of the futures curve in real time. For each evaluation window, model parameters are estimated using only the training subsample. These parameters are then held fixed while the model is applied to the subsequent test period. At each test date, the one-step-ahead predicted latent state, formed before observing contemporaneous futures prices, is used to construct the model-implied futures curve across maturities. This predicted curve is directly compared to the realized futures prices observed in the market, allowing for a clear visual assessment of the model’s real-time pricing performance.

**Forecast versus update: interpreting the two model-implied curves.**\
For each test date, the visualization overlays two model-implied curves: a dashed curve representing the one-step-ahead out-of-sample forecast and a solid curve representing the filtered estimate after observing the contemporaneous futures prices. The forecast curve is based on the predicted state at∣t−1​ and reflects the model’s genuine out-of-sample implication of the futures term structure using training-only parameter estimates. The filtered curve, by contrast, incorporates the current observation and shows how the model updates its latent state once new information arrives. The distance between the two curves therefore captures the real-time forecast error and the magnitude of the state revision induced by incoming market data, providing insight into both predictive accuracy and model adaptability.

**Relation to Schwartz and Smith (2000).**\
This exercise closely aligns with the state-space interpretation underlying Schwartz and Smith (2000), in which futures prices are viewed as noisy observations of latent economic factors driving the term structure. While the original paper focuses primarily on estimation and valuation implications, the present analysis extends the framework by explicitly examining the model’s real-time out-of-sample performance at the level of the entire futures curve. By showing that parameters estimated on historical data can generate economically sensible one-step-ahead forecasts across maturities, and by illustrating how these forecasts are subsequently updated by new observations, this extension provides a natural and conceptually consistent complement to the original methodology, reinforcing the empirical relevance and structural coherence of the Schwartz–Smith model.

```{r step8_visuals}

###############################################################################
# STEP 8 (ADD-ON) — Visual OOS term structures from stored Step 8 outputs
#   Forecast:  a_{t|t-1}  (kf_te$at)   -> true one-step-ahead OOS
#   Filtered:  a_{t|t}    (kf_te$att)  -> after seeing y_t
###############################################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tibble)
  library(dplyr)
  library(cowplot)
})

# --- choose evenly spaced indices in the TEST sample ---
.pick_spaced_idx <- function(nT, n = 6) {
  if (nT <= n) return(seq_len(nT))
  unique(round(seq(1, nT, length.out = n)))
}

# --- build smooth curve for a given state (chi, xi) and theta ---
.curve_from_state <- function(theta, chi, xi, tau_grid) {
  A_grid <- A_fun(
    T          = tau_grid,
    kappa      = theta$kappa,
    mu_star    = theta$mu_star,
    sigma_chi  = theta$sigma_chi,
    sigma_xi   = theta$sigma_xi,
    rho        = theta$rho,
    lambda_chi = theta$lambda_chi
  )
  A_grid + exp(-theta$kappa * tau_grid) * chi + xi
}

# --- one panel: observed vs forecast vs filtered at a specific TEST index j ---
.oos_panel_one <- function(res, j, in_levels = FALSE) {
  stopifnot(is.list(res), !is.null(res$kf_te), !is.null(res$ss_te))

  theta <- res$theta_train
  kf    <- res$kf_te
  ss    <- res$ss_te

  # observation + maturities for this test week
  y_obs_log <- as.numeric(res$Y_test[, j])
  tau_pts   <- as.numeric(res$Tau_test[, j])
  Z_t       <- ss$Zt[, , j]
  c_t       <- ss$ct[, j]

  # states:
  a_pred <- as.numeric(kf$at[,  j])   # a_{t|t-1}  (true OOS forecast state)
  a_filt <- as.numeric(kf$att[, j])   # a_{t|t}    (after seeing y_t)

  # predicted & filtered fitted values at traded maturities
  y_pred_log <- as.numeric(c_t + Z_t %*% a_pred)
  y_filt_log <- as.numeric(c_t + Z_t %*% a_filt)

  # smooth maturity grid
  tau_grid <- seq(0, max(tau_pts, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 200)

  y_pred_grid_log <- .curve_from_state(theta, a_pred[1], a_pred[2], tau_grid)
  y_filt_grid_log <- .curve_from_state(theta, a_filt[1], a_filt[2], tau_grid)

  # levels vs logs
  if (isTRUE(in_levels)) {
    y_obs  <- exp(y_obs_log)
    y_pred <- exp(y_pred_log)
    y_filt <- exp(y_filt_log)
    y_pred_grid <- exp(y_pred_grid_log)
    y_filt_grid <- exp(y_filt_grid_log)
    ylab <- "Price (levels)"
  } else {
    y_obs  <- y_obs_log
    y_pred <- y_pred_log
    y_filt <- y_filt_log
    y_pred_grid <- y_pred_grid_log
    y_filt_grid <- y_filt_grid_log
    ylab <- "log price"
  }

  df_obs <- tibble(maturity_m = 12 * tau_pts, value = y_obs)
  df_pts <- tibble(
    maturity_m = 12 * tau_pts,
    Forecast   = y_pred,
    Filtered   = y_filt
  ) |> tidyr::pivot_longer(-maturity_m, names_to = "series", values_to = "value")

  df_line <- tibble(
    maturity_m = 12 * tau_grid,
    Forecast   = y_pred_grid,
    Filtered   = y_filt_grid
  ) |> tidyr::pivot_longer(-maturity_m, names_to = "series", values_to = "value")

  date_lab <- if (!is.null(res$dates_test)) format(res$dates_test[j], "%d %b %Y") else paste("Test", j)

  ggplot() +
    # smooth curves (Forecast vs Filtered)
    geom_line(data = df_line, aes(maturity_m, value, linetype = series),
          colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
    # observed points (add to legend via shape mapping)
    geom_point(data = df_obs, aes(maturity_m, value, shape = "Observed (log futures)"),
              fill = "white", colour = "black",
              size = 2.6, stroke = 0.9) +
    # dots at traded maturities for forecast & filtered
    geom_point(data = df_pts, aes(maturity_m, value, shape = series),
               colour = "black", size = 1.9) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Forecast = "dashed", Filtered = "solid")) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(
                      "Filtered" = 19,
                      "Forecast" = 1,
                      "Observed (log futures)" = 21
                    )) +
    labs(
      title = date_lab,
      x = "Maturity (months)", y = ylab,
      shape = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) 
}

# --- grid wrapper like Step 6 ---
plot_oos_grid_from_step8 <- function(res, n_panels = 6, in_levels = FALSE, savepath = NULL) {
  nT <- ncol(res$Y_test)
  idx <- .pick_spaced_idx(nT, n = n_panels)

  # Build plots
  plots <- lapply(idx, function(j) .oos_panel_one(res, j, in_levels = in_levels))

  # Extract ONE legend from the first plot
  leg <- cowplot::get_legend(
    plots[[1]] + theme(legend.position = "top")
  )

  # Remove legends from all panels
  plots <- lapply(plots, function(p) p + theme(legend.position = "none"))

  # Arrange grid
  grid <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = plots, ncol = 3)

  ttl  <- if (!is.null(res$meta$section_name)) res$meta$section_name else "OOS Visual"
  top  <- cowplot::ggdraw() + cowplot::draw_label(ttl, fontface = "bold", x = 0, hjust = 0)

  # Combine: title + legend + grid
  fig <- cowplot::plot_grid(
    top,
    leg,
    grid,
    ncol = 1,
    rel_heights = c(0.08, 0.10, 0.82)
  )

  print(fig)

  if (!is.null(savepath)) {
    dir.create(dirname(savepath), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    ggsave(savepath, fig, width = 14, height = max(6, ceiling(length(plots)/3)*2.2), dpi = 300)
  }

  invisible(fig)
}


# ---- Example calls (uncomment) ----
plot_oos_grid_from_step8(res_norm1)
plot_oos_grid_from_step8(res_norm2)
plot_oos_grid_from_step8(res_cris1)
plot_oos_grid_from_step8(res_cris2)


```

## Step 9: Comparison with SS2000 Tables 2 & 3

This final step compares the full-timeline replication results directly to the benchmark findings reported in Schwartz and Smith (2000). The goal is to assess whether an independently implemented version of the same model reproduces the key empirical magnitudes documented in the original study.

First, the estimated structural parameters are aligned with the layout of Table 2 in SS2000. Overall, the core parameters governing mean reversion, factor volatilities, and measurement error are of similar order of magnitude to those reported in the paper, indicating that the model captures comparable dynamics in futures prices. At the same time, some differences emerge, particularly for the long-term mean level and the maturity-specific measurement errors, which is expected given the longer sample period and updated data used in this replication.

Second, the fit of the model is evaluated using innovation-based error measures analogous to those reported in Table 3 of SS2000. The results show that pricing errors generally decrease with maturity and remain small in absolute terms, consistent with the patterns documented in the original paper. While the longer sample and different market environments naturally lead to deviations from the exact SS2000 values, the overall structure of pricing accuracy across maturities is preserved.

Taken together, these comparisons suggest that the full-timeline replication successfully reproduces the main empirical features of Schwartz and Smith (2000), while also reflecting differences attributable to sample extension and evolving market conditions rather than methodological inconsistencies.

```{r step9}
#############################################################################
# STEP 9 — Compare the estimates with SS2000 Tables 2 & 3
#############################################################################

stopifnot(all(c("kappa","mu","mu_star","sigma_chi","sigma_xi","rho","lambda_chi","sigma_obs_vec") %in% names(theta_hat)))
lambda_xi_implied <- theta_hat$mu - theta_hat$mu_star

# --- 1) Estimated parameters ----------------------------------------------------
my_params <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c(
    "kappa","mu","mu_star","sigma_chi","sigma_xi","rho","lambda_chi","lambda_xi",
    paste0("sigma_obs_", c("1m","5m","9m","13m","17m"))
  ),
  estimate = c(
    theta_hat$kappa, theta_hat$mu, theta_hat$mu_star,
    theta_hat$sigma_chi, theta_hat$sigma_xi, theta_hat$rho,
    theta_hat$lambda_chi, lambda_xi_implied,
    as.numeric(theta_hat$sigma_obs_vec)
  )
)

# Attach SEs if available.
# Note: the SE table uses sigma_obs_1..sigma_obs_5, while we label them by maturity
# (1m, 5m, 9m, 13m, 17m) to match the Table 2 layout we print.
if (exists("parameter_se") && is.data.frame(parameter_se)) {

  parameter_se_step9 <- parameter_se |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      parameter = dplyr::case_when(
        parameter == "sigma_obs_1" ~ "sigma_obs_1m",
        parameter == "sigma_obs_2" ~ "sigma_obs_5m",
        parameter == "sigma_obs_3" ~ "sigma_obs_9m",
        parameter == "sigma_obs_4" ~ "sigma_obs_13m",
        parameter == "sigma_obs_5" ~ "sigma_obs_17m",
        TRUE ~ parameter
      )
    )

  my_params <- dplyr::left_join(
    my_params,
    dplyr::select(parameter_se_step9, parameter, se),
    by = "parameter"
  )

} else {
  my_params$se <- NA_real_
}


# --- 2) Paper values (SS2000 Table 2) -------------------------------------------
paper_params <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c(
    "kappa","mu", "mu_star","sigma_chi","sigma_xi","rho","lambda_chi",
    paste0("sigma_obs_", c("1m","5m","9m","13m","17m"))
  ),
  paper_val = c(
    1.49,
    -0.0125,
    0.0115,
    0.286,
    0.145,
    0.300,
    0.157,
    0.042, 0.006, 0.003, 0.000, 0.004
  )
)

compare_params <- dplyr::left_join(my_params, paper_params, by = "parameter") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    abs_diff   = estimate - paper_val,
    rel_diff   = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(paper_val) & paper_val != 0, abs_diff / paper_val, NA_real_),
    within_2se = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(se), abs(abs_diff) <= 2 * se, NA)
  )

# --- 3) OOS comparison (based on Step 8 outputs) ----------------------------
# Step 8 returns per-section results in objects such as res_norm1, res_norm2, ...
# We compare the TRAIN in-sample RMSE (innovations) with the paper's Table 3 SDs
# as a rough calibration, and report the OOS RMSE as additional information.

stopifnot(exists("res_norm1") || exists("step8_multi_outputs"))

# Reference OOS section for the comparison (first normal window)
res_ref <- if (exists("res_norm1") && !is.null(res_norm1)) res_norm1 else step8_multi_outputs$normal_1
stopifnot(!is.null(res_ref), !is.null(res_ref$compare_tbl))

fit_my <- res_ref$compare_tbl %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    maturity = maturity,
    rmse_in_sample_train = RMSE_in_sample_train,
    rmse_oos             = RMSE_OOS,
    oos_minus_in         = OOS_minus_in_sample
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
  maturity = dplyr::case_when(
    # already in paper units
    maturity %in% c("1m","5m","9m","13m","17m") ~ maturity,

    # generic index labels from Step 8 when ranks are absent
    maturity %in% c("1","1m") ~ "1m",
    maturity %in% c("2","2m") ~ "5m",
    maturity %in% c("3","3m") ~ "9m",
    maturity %in% c("4","4m") ~ "13m",
    maturity %in% c("5","5m") ~ "17m",

    # just in case maturity labels came through like "CL1", "CL5", etc.
    grepl("^CL\\d+$", maturity) ~ paste0(sub("^CL", "", maturity), "m"),

    TRUE ~ maturity
  )
)


paper_fit <- tibble::tibble(
  maturity  = c("1m","5m","9m","13m","17m"),
  sd_paper  = c(0.0414, 0.0044, 0.0025, 0.0000, 0.0035),
  mae_paper = c(0.0314, 0.0035, 0.0020, 0.0000, 0.0028)
)

compare_fit <- dplyr::left_join(fit_my, paper_fit, by = "maturity") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    sd_abs_diff = rmse_in_sample_train - sd_paper,
    sd_rel_diff = dplyr::if_else(sd_paper != 0, sd_abs_diff / sd_paper, NA_real_)
  )


# --- 4) Table 3 replication using full-sample innovations vt from kf_hat ----
stopifnot(exists("kf_hat"), is.list(kf_hat), !is.null(kf_hat$vt))

vt <- kf_hat$vt
stopifnot(all(dim(vt) == dim(Y)))

# Restore missingness so stats ignore weeks where contract is missing
vt[is.na(Y)] <- NA_real_


# Compute Table-3 style moments per contract
tab3_my_by_contract <- tibble::tibble(
  contract = rownames(Y),
  mean_error = rowMeans(vt, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd_error   = apply(vt, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
  mae_error  = rowMeans(abs(vt), na.rm = TRUE)
)

# Map contracts to paper maturities (CL1, CL5, CL9, CL13, CL17 -> 1m,5m,9m,13m,17m)
tab3_my <- tab3_my_by_contract |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl_num = suppressWarnings(as.integer(stringr::str_extract(contract, "(?<=CL)\\d+"))),
    maturity = dplyr::case_when(
      cl_num == 1  ~ "1m",
      cl_num == 5  ~ "5m",
      cl_num == 9  ~ "9m",
      cl_num == 13 ~ "13m",
      cl_num == 17 ~ "17m",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(maturity)) |>
  dplyr::select(maturity, mean_error, sd_error, mae_error)

# Paper Table 3 values (Futures Data)
tab3_paper <- tibble::tibble(
  maturity    = c("1m","5m","9m","13m","17m"),
  mean_paper  = c(-0.0053, 0.0005, -0.0002, 0.0000, 0.0000),
  sd_paper    = c( 0.0414, 0.0044,  0.0025, 0.0000, 0.0035),
  mae_paper   = c( 0.0314, 0.0035,  0.0020, 0.0000, 0.0028)
)

# Compare the Table 3 statistics with the paper's
tab3_compare <- dplyr::left_join(tab3_my, tab3_paper, by = "maturity") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mean_diff = mean_error - mean_paper,
    sd_diff   = sd_error   - sd_paper,
    mae_diff  = mae_error  - mae_paper
  )


print(compare_params)
print(compare_fit)
print(tab3_compare)

step9_outputs <- list(
  parameters_comparison = compare_params,
  oos_fit_comparison    = compare_fit,
  table3_comparison     = tab3_compare
)

```
